from_notes: Synapse: The junction where one neuron's axon connects with another neuron's dendrite to transfer impulses.
x: A synapse is the junction (gap) between two neurons across which the impulse passes, usually by neurotransmitters. The dendrite receives and the axon carries the impulse; the impulse is the signal itself, not a gap. (Biology PYQ: moved to book 5 row 1.)
source: PMF General Science 01 p.65; PMF General Science 03 p.43 ('Synapse: a junction between two neurons...')

from_notes: Right Livelihood Award ('Alternative Nobel Prize') - est. 1980 by Jakob von Uexkull.
x: The Right Livelihood Award, called the 'Alternative Nobel Prize', was set up in 1980 by Jakob von Uexkull to honour practical solutions to urgent global problems (environment, human rights, peace). 1970, 1990 and 2000 are wrong.
source: rightlivelihood.org/about-us (fetched: founded by Jakob von Uexkull; 'Standing up for human courage since 1980'); app notes 6:91 sub 4

from_notes: The Vegetarian | Han Kang (tr. Deborah Smith) | 2016 Man Booker International
x: Han Kang (South Korea, Nobel Literature 2024) won the 2016 Man Booker International Prize, now the International Booker Prize, with translator Deborah Smith for 'The Vegetarian'. The novel did not win a Pulitzer or a PEN America award, so 'more than one' is wrong.

from_notes: Bhanu Athaiya – first Indian winner for 'Gandhi' (1983, Best Costume Design).
x: Bhanu Athaiya became the first Indian to win an Oscar: Best Costume Design for 'Gandhi' at the 1983 Academy Awards (film of 1982). Satyajit Ray got an Honorary Oscar only in 1992, and Mrinal Sen, Bimal Roy and Chetan Anand never won one.
source: Praveen CA-360 Mar 2026 magazine p.9; PMF Lens Mar 2026 ('Bhanu Athaiya was India's first Oscar winner for Gandhi'); app notes 6:92 sub 2

from_notes: 2018 Guillermo Cano Prize - Mahmoud Abu Zeid ('Shawkan'), Egyptian photojournalist (given 2 May).
x: Mahmoud Abu Zeid ('Shawkan'), the 2018 UNESCO/Guillermo Cano World Press Freedom Prize laureate, is an Egyptian photojournalist. He was jailed after covering the 2013 Rabaa sit-in in Cairo and was the first Egyptian to win the prize. He is not from Israel, Iraq or Iran. (The 2026 prize went to the Sudanese Journalists Syndicate.)
source: web search 'UNESCO 2018 Guillermo Cano prize Mahmoud Abu Zeid' (news.un.org 2018/04/1007942; english.ahram.org.eg: Egypt's imprisoned journalist Shawkan); Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.49 (2026 prize); app notes 6:92 sub 6
evidence: Local library: Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.49 and Praveen CA-360 May 2026 p.12 give only the 2026 laureate and est. 1997
